claims.text: AI Agents are modular systems driven and enabled by LLMs and LIMs for task-specific automation.
Agentic AI systems represent a paradigm shift marked by multi-agent collaboration, dynamic task decomposition, persistent memory, and coordinated autonomy.
AI Agents enable applications in customer support, scheduling, and data summarization.
Agentic AI enables deployments in research automation, robotic coordination, and medical decision support.

evidence.description: Abstract characterizes AI Agents as modular systems driven and enabled by LLMs and LIMs for task-specific automation.
Abstract contrasts Agentic AI with AI Agents as a paradigm shift defined by multi-agent collaboration, dynamic task decomposition, persistent memory, and coordinated autonomy.
Abstract outlines application domains enabled by AI Agents including customer support, scheduling, and data summarization.
Abstract lists Agentic AI deployments in research automation, robotic coordination, and medical decision support.

methodologies.name: Taxonomic Review and Chronological Comparative Analysis
methodologies.description: A systematic review evaluating architectural evolution, operational mechanisms, interaction styles, and autonomy levels across AI agents and agentic AI.

limitations.text: AI agent and Agentic AI paradigms suffer from challenges including hallucination, brittleness, emergent behavior, and coordination failure.
